subject: Airly onboarding: model shortlist, context needs, and token sizing
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
To: Sara Hu <sara@airly.ai>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 21 Oct 2025 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Airly onboarding: model shortlist, context needs, and token sizing
Attachments: airly_poc_token_estimates.xlsx (spreadsheet)

Hi Sara —

Thanks again for the call today. Per our discussion, I put together a short initial proposal for the model shortlist and rough token-volume estimates to help the implementation team size capacity for the pilot. The attached spreadsheet has the line-item token math; key asks below so we can lock the right model tier for the PoC: 

- Peak concurrent requests (QPS) during business hours (estimate): what do you expect for the initial pilot (week 1) and for month 1 after launch?
- Typical prompt/context lengths: are you sending single-turn prompts (~100 tokens) or multi-turn conversation windows (500–2,000 tokens)? If you have a canonical example, paste it and we will simulate.
- SLA/latency target: is 250–500ms per token acceptable, or do you need sub-200ms for the user-facing flows?

Notes on model shortlist and tradeoffs (quick):
- Opt B (Llama 2 13B quantized) — good latency/cost balance for ~1k–3k tokens; recommended for chat flows where hallucination risk is moderate.
- Opt C (Redwood-medium-13B float16) — higher quality, higher cost; recommended if you need instruction-following with long context (>1k tokens) and lower temperature.
- Safety fallback: we recommend a small 3B reranker for short canonical prompts to reduce generation cost when exact matches exist.

Next steps: can you confirm the three bullets above by EOD Thursday? Monica (CC) will pick up once we have numbers and run a quick cost/throughput sim for Dedicated vs Hosted.

Thanks —
Jonas

Subject: Re: Airly onboarding: model shortlist, context needs, and token sizing

Thanks Jonas — great summary and appreciated the options. Quick answers below: 

- Peak requests: Pilot week we expect 120–150 QPS at peak (internal test). Month 1 target is 220–300 QPS (gradual ramp).
- Context: most user journeys are short (300–450 tokens), but support chat and summary endpoints will send 1,200–1,800 token windows. We have one workflow that needs a 3k token context for historical context; for the pilot we can truncate to 1.5k but plan to unlock the full window by month 2.
- Latency: user-facing UI needs <= 400ms per API response for 95th percentile. Background jobs (batch summarization) can be slower.

I attached a sample prompt in-line below (sanitized). Also flagging that our security team may request an air-gapped/private deployment for some customer datasets later in the year.

Sample prompt: 
"Given the user's purchase history and last three support messages, suggest the top 3 troubleshooting steps and the best next-action phrase to present in the UI."

If you can sketch the Dedicated pool we should target and expected monthly token run-rate for pilot vs M1 that would be super helpful.

—Sara
Sara Hu
Head of Product
Airly Inc.

Attachments: model_shortlist_diagram.png (png)

Sara — perfect, thanks for the numbers and the example prompt. I routed this to Monica and Grace so CS/implementation can size the Dedicated pool and the fallback policies. Quick answers and recommended pilot config below: 

- Recommended pilot capacity (Dedicated reserved): 4x A100-equivalent workers with autoscale to +2 for bursts. At your peak M1 QPS (300) and mixed context (avg ~700 tokens with some 1.5k windows) this maps to ~1.8M tokens/day for pilot and ~5.5M tokens/day at steady month-1 ramp (see attached workbook for token math).
- Model slate: start pilot with Redwood-medium-13B float16 for the long-context endpoints (summary & multi-turn), and Llama2-13B-quant for high-QPS short prompts. Configure a light reranker (3B) for deterministic UI flows to cut generation tokens when matches exist.
- Context handling: enable prefix/KV cache for repeated history (support chat). For the 3k window workflow, we'll implement truncation to 1.5k for pilot and evaluate QPS/latency; unlocking full 3k requires memory-tuned kernels and a higher tier plan.
- Latency: with the above config we expect 95th percentile per-response latencies around 300–420ms for user-facing endpoints.

Action items: 
1) Monica to run Dedicated vs Hosted cost sim and share a single-slide recommendation (Monica: can you target EOD tomorrow?).
2) Sara to confirm whether the 3k window must be supported for pilot or can be deferred to M2.
3) Grace to schedule a short infra sync (30 min) with Airly ops to discuss VPC/network and any air-gap constraints.

If everyone is OK I will update the attached workbook with the Dedicated sizing assumptions and a suggested rollout timeline (pilot: 2 weeks, M1 ramp: +4 weeks).

Thanks —
Jonas

> 
> - Recommended pilot capacity (Dedicated reserved): 4x A100-equivalent workers with autoscale to +2 for bursts. At your peak M1 QPS (300) and mixed context (avg ~700 tokens with some 1.5k windows) this maps to ~1.8M tokens/day for pilot and ~5.5M tokens/day at steady month-1 ramp (see attached workbook for token math).

Thanks — I pulled the workbook and did a quick sanity check. A couple of internal notes before I publish the single-slide: 
- The 1.8M/day pilot estimate assumes 50% of requests are short prompts (<=450 tokens) and 20% are long summaries (~1.5k). If Airly's actual distribution skews heavier on long windows we should add +30% capacity buffer.
- Reranker savings: if the reranker achieves a 35% short-circuit rate on canonical prompts, estimated token spend drops ~22% (we'll include that sensitivity line on the slide).
- Security: re: air-gapped/private deployment, we should prepare a short checklist for their security team (KMS integration, audit logs, egress rules). Grace, can you own the VPC checklist and propose an initial timeline?

I'll have the cost/throughput slide and a concise implementation checklist by EOD. Planned outbound to Airly ops will include a proposed infra sync time (Mon-Fri 9–11 PT).

Monica Patel
